title: Sine of a Sum: Compound Angles Explained Simply | PUC Maths Class 11
description:
Is sin(30° + 60°) the same as sin 30° + sin 60°? The first is sin 90° = 1. The second is 1.366, higher than any point on a circle of radius 1. So how do we find the sine or cosine of a sum? In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Maths (NCERT Chapter 3, Trigonometric Functions) we build the compound-angle formulae from one unit circle.

You will watch the NCERT proof come alive: four points on the unit circle and a chord that turns through the angle y to land exactly on another chord, then the distance formula turns that into cos(x + y) = cos x cos y - sin x sin y. From it we get cos(x - y), sin(x ± y) and tan(x + y), and a live slider shows the formula matching the real value while sin x + sin y never does. Two pause-and-think questions, the rule "sine mixes and keeps the sign, cosine pairs and flips it", a worked example (the exact value of sin 15°), the exam trap with the sign of cos(x + y), an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11 and JEE Main students.
